==English==

===Alternative forms===

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*gerbʰ-}}
{{bor+|en|fr|programme}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|programma||a proclamation, edict}}, from {{der|en|grc|πρόγραμμα||a written public notice, an edict}}, from {{m|grc|προγράφω||to set forth as a public notice}}, from {{m|grc|πρό||before}} + {{m|grc|γράφω||to write}}. {{doublet|en|programma}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|activities}} A set of structured [[activity|activities]]; a [[plan]] of action.
#: {{hypo|en|curriculum}}
#: {{cot|en|agenda|schedule}}
#: {{collocation|en|get with the '''program'''}}
#: {{ux|en|Our '''program''' for today’s exercise class includes swimming and jogging.}}
# {{senseid|en|leaflet}} A leaflet listing information about a play, game or other activity.
#: {{ux|en|The '''program''' consisted of ads for restaurants and the credits of everyone connected with the play.}}
# {{senseid|en|politics}} {{lb|en|politics}} A set of principal goals which someone, especially a political party or candidate, supports.
#: {{syn|en|platform}}
# {{senseid|en|broadcasting}} {{lb|en|broadcasting}} A performance of a [[show]] or other [[broadcast]] on [[radio]] or [[television]].
#: {{ux|en|Tonight’s '''program''' was hosted by Johnny Carson.}}
# {{senseid|en|computing}} {{lb|en|computing}} A [[computer program]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''program''' runs on both [[Linux]] and Microsoft [[Windows]].}}
# {{senseid|en|mindset}} {{lb|en|especially|in the phrase "[[get with the program]]"}} A particular mindset or [[method]] of doing things.
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1988|title=w:Die Hard
|passage=<small>Ellis:</small> Come on, John, why don’t you get with the '''program''' and tell him where the detonators are?}}
# {{senseid|en|music}} {{lb|en|music|computing}} A [[custom]] [[tracklist]].
#: {{co|en|'''program''' playback|playing tracks in a custom order}}

====Usage notes====
* Usage of ''program'' and ''programme'':
** US: ''program'' is the only spelling normally used, no matter which sense it is used in.
** UK: ''programme'' is used in all cases except for computer code, in which case ''program'' has generally superseded ''programme'' since the 1960s. However, ''programme'' is still occasionally used for computer code, and some even consider it the only correct spelling also for this meaning.
** Canada: both ''program'' and ''programme'' are used, but ''program'' is more common.
** Australia: ''program'' is endorsed by the Macquarie Dictionary and is frequently used in both formal and informal settings.
** New Zealand: ''programme'' is favoured by New Zealand dictionaries, and is endorsed by government usage; ''program'' is rarely seen outside the computing meaning.
** Singapore and Malaysia: ''program'' and ''programme'' are interchangeable (the latter is more common), but only ''program'' is used in computing.

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L24}}
{{en-verb|++,+!<l:rare>}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To enter a program or other [[instruction]]s into (a [[computer]] or other electronic [[device]]) to instruct it to do a particular task.
#: {{ux|en|He '''programmed''' the DVR to record his favorite show.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To develop (software) by writing program code.
#: {{ux|en|I '''programmed''' a small game as a demonstration.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To put together the [[schedule]] of an [[event]].
#: {{ux|en|Mary will '''program''' Tuesday’s festivities.}}
# {{lb|en|broadcasting}} To schedule the [[programming]]; to determine what will be [[broadcast]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1956|author=United States. Congress. Senate|title=Hearings|volume=5|page=2586
|passage=We '''program''' for special audience groups, too, as shown by our Mexican language program each Sunday morning.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to [[automatic]]ally behave in a particular way.
#: {{ux|en|The lab rat was '''programmed''' to press the lever when the bell rang.}}
